corrections.source_says: The medians favor CommSketch and the raw p is .019. But the paper applies Holm correction across the six creativity-support items, and Expressiveness does not survive it (p_Holm = .097). The paper concludes that the ratings do not establish an improvement. no_clear_difference fits the paper's own test and reading. If the field keeps the sign of the medians, the record should say the difference rests on the raw p only.
corrections.quote: Median Expressiveness ratings were higher, although the difference was not significant after Holm correction (pHolm = .097). ... the ratings do not establish a general improvement in perceived expressiveness.
corrections.locator: p. 14, Section 5.2, first paragraph; p. 9, Table 4

corrections.source_says: The paper names two central outcomes: perceived creativity support and the experience of human-AI collaboration, both measured by the post-task questionnaires. It reports the questionnaire results first and uses interaction-sequence coding and interviews to contextualise them. S1-O1 (a collaboration item) and S1-O2 (a creativity-support item) belong to these two families, so paper_primary fits at the family level (no single item is singled out). S1-O3 (Design Intent coding) is contextual, so secondary fits.
corrections.quote: We organise the results around the two central outcomes of the study: designers’ perceived creativity support and their experience of human–AI collaboration.

corrections.source_says: For each item, Tables 4 and 5 print both arms' medians with first and third quartiles, U, the rank-biserial correlation δ, and raw and Holm-adjusted p, with n = 12 per condition. The paper names δ as its effect size, so the list should include standardized_effect (a rank-biserial correlation, not a standardized mean difference). p_value_only is wrong because the p-value is not the only statistic. No means, SDs, standard errors, or intervals are printed.
corrections.quote: Descriptive statistics are reported as medians (Md) and interquartile ranges (IQR), with rank-biserial correlation (δ) reported as the effect size.
corrections.locator: p. 6, Section 3.6.1; p. 9, Table 4; p. 11, Table 5

corrections.source_says: The counts are printed in the text of Section 4.1.1 as well as on the bars of Figure 5, and the form's own locator cites both, so they are not figure-only. The paper prints each arm's count of participants out of n = 12 and no test, standard error, or interval. The closest listed code is arm_means_sds_ns (counts out of 12 per arm), with a note that no SD is printed.
corrections.quote: Experience-related intentions were expressed by nine CommSketch participants, compared with two Sketch-Only participants.

confirmed: Version: the p. 1 margin stamp reads arXiv:2609.37813v1 [cs.HC] 29 Sep 2026. The arXiv API lists v1 as the only version (published and updated 2026-09-29, comment 'work in progress', no journal reference). The ACM placeholders (Conference acronym 'XX, 2018, DOI XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX) and the 19 pages match the form (pp. 1-2).
Title and the four authors (Weiyan Shi, Darryl Lim, Geraldine Quek, Kenny Tsu Wei Choo, all Singapore University of Technology and Design) match the document (p. 1).

No supplement, data or code link, preregistration, funding, or company statement appears. The only body URLs are placeholder DOIs. Appendix A with codebook Tables 6-8 is on pp. 17-19, as the form says.

Assignment quote is verbatim: 'Participants were randomly assigned to Sketch-Only (n = 12) or CommSketch (n = 12).' (p. 5, Section 3.4). Both arms used the same prototype, task, AI model, prompting strategy, and generation pipeline (p. 4, Section 3.1), so criterion 1 is met as an ai_design contrast with CommSketch as treatment. lab_rct fits the one-hour, researcher-run session (p. 5, Section 3.5).

Counts: 24 people randomized and 24 analyzed. Tables 4 and 5 and Figures 4, 5, 7, 9, and 10 all use n = 12 per condition, and no exclusions are stated. 24 is below 50, so criterion 2 is not met (p. 5; pp. 8-12).

No creativity or diversity score on the designs: outcomes are six CSI-adapted items and seven collaboration items on seven-point scales (p. 6, Section 3.6.1) plus qualitative coding of Design Intent, Human Follow-up, and Creative Agency (p. 7, Table 3). The paper lists evaluating 'the creativity of resulting designs' as future work (p. 14, Section 5.3). Criterion 3 not met, context_class none, and core no are right.

S1-O1 reported string matches Table 5 (p. 11): Alignment Sketch-Only 3.5 [3.00, 5.00] vs CommSketch 6.0 [5.75, 7.00], U = 22.5, δ = 0.69, p_raw = .004, p_Holm = .028. Holm runs across the 7 collaboration items (Table 5 note; p. 6, Section 3.6.1).

S1-O2 reported string matches Table 4 (p. 9): Expressiveness 4.5 [4.00, 5.00] vs 6.0 [5.00, 7.00], U = 32.0, δ = 0.56, p_raw = .019, p_Holm = .097. All six Holm-adjusted p-values are .091 or higher (Table 4), so 'no Creativity Support Index item survived Holm correction' holds.

S1-O3 reported string matches: Form 12 vs 12, Function 12 vs 10, Experience 9 vs 2 (CommSketch vs Sketch-Only), with no test (p. 8, Section 4.1.1; p. 9, Figure 5). Two coders reached Cohen's κ = .79 for Design Intent (p. 8). Speech counted as evidence only in CommSketch (p. 7, Table 3 caption), as measure_detail says.
One-line finding is exact: alignment median 6.0 vs 3.5, U = 22.5, δ = 0.69, p_Holm = .028 (p. 11, Table 5), with no CSI item significant after Holm correction (p. 9, Table 4; p. 8, Section 4.1).

AI tool: gemini-2.5-flash gives the interpretation (p. 4, Section 3.3.2). Gemini 2.5 Flash and Gemini 2.5 Flash Image handle text and image generation (p. 5, Section 3.3.2). Image generation was 77.4% (Sketch-Only) and 86.3% (CommSketch) of AI-use events (p. 10, Section 4.1.3), which supports the image_generation role code.

Task: 'freely ideate toaster designs within 30 minutes' (p. 5, Section 3.5), done individually (p. 14, Section 6) on an iPad Pro 13-inch with Apple Pencil (p. 4, Section 3.3.1). The session lasted about one hour, in stages of 10, 30, 5, and 15 minutes (p. 5, Section 3.5; p. 6, Table 2).

Participants: Table 1 lists 18 undergraduates, 4 master's or PhD students, and 2 practitioners (S3 automotive designer, C11 UI designer), so population mixed fits. Pay was about USD 7.8. The paper does not say where participants were recruited, and the form says so (p. 5, Section 3.4; p. 6, Table 1).
sample_overlap empty is right: the paper reports no reuse of participants. The formative study (N = 6) and the Wizard-of-Oz study (N = 20) it cites are prior work (p. 3, Section 2.3).
summary: All printed numbers, the counts (24 randomized and analyzed, 12 per arm), the design class, and the eligibility verdict match the arXiv v1 PDF, and the one study randomizes people between two generative-AI configurations but scores no creativity or diversity on their designs, so has_randomized_people_study is false. Four coding fields need fixes: the Expressiveness direction should be no_clear_difference (p_Holm = .097), primary should follow the paper's two named central outcomes, the questionnaire contrasts should list δ as a standardized effect instead of p_value_only, and the Design Intent counts are printed in the text, not only in a figure.
